title: Contribution + Deprecation Pipeline and RFC Pathway for UI Primitives
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Our component library has grown organically and contributions are inconsistent: missing rationale, incomplete accessibility notes, and unclear retirement paths. This ticket proposes a lightweight, enforceable contribution pipeline and an RFC pathway specifically tailored to UI primitives (tokens, buttons, tables, charts). Goals: 1) Create a short RFC template for design/engineering trade-offs, 2) Establish a reviewer checklist that gates additions/changes (accessibility, acceptance tests, migration notes), 3) Define a four-stage deprecation lifecycle with SLA-like timelines and communication templates, 4) Add CI checks and PR templates so the pipeline is executable, 5) Provide migration recipe archetypes and an owner-assignment rubric.
acceptance_criteria: RFC template saved in Confluence + linked in PR template
Review checklist added to design README and enforced as 'must-address' in PR description
Deprecation lifecycle defined with sample timelines (announced, deprecated, scheduled removal, removed) and communication templates
Two example migrations (tokens -> new token scale, legacy table -> v2 API) documented with code/figma examples
CI linter rule added that flags component PRs without required checklist items (accessibility, screenshots, migration note)
decision: Adopt a pragmatic RFC-first approach for any public API change to primitives. RFCs live in Confluence with a single-line summary added to the PR. Deprecation will be explicit, minimum 60-day notice for client-facing tokens/components, and removal gated by owner sign-off and migration support. Lightweight automation (PR templates + GH action) will be used to enforce checklist completion; stricter enforcement can be phased in after two cycles.
